statement: Let $T$ be a triangulation of the 2-sphere with at most 12 vertices and $H(T)$ its vertex-face incidence graph. Is $H(T)$ Sidorenko for every such $T$?

source.reference: This record's probes complex-structure-1 and small-spheres-1: the 2026 counterexample is the incidence graph of a 13-vertex triangulated sphere, and its combinatorial hypotheses hold for no sphere with at most 12 vertices and for exactly two with 13.

observation: The three regular deltahedra give weakly norming incidence graphs; bipyramids (suspensions of a polygon) give Sidorenko incidence graphs by doubling a cone, which has a vertex complete to the other part; the 9,150 spheres with 4 to 12 vertices are outside the counterexample's hypotheses. Whether the threshold 13 belongs to the Sidorenko property or only to the construction is not known; the pattern is computational and has no structural explanation yet.
neighbours: Is the incidence graph of the second 13-vertex sphere satisfying the hypotheses non-Sidorenko?
Incidence graphs of triangulated Mobius bands (odd twisted blow-ups)
Incidence graphs of triangulated surfaces of higher genus
notes: A finite family question whose threshold comes from one construction.
